mysteries.question: Does Gwenyth share your feelings, or are you truly dreaming in vain?
mysteries.answer: Gwenyth is desperately unhappy in her marriage to the abusive Aldous and feels a deep, secret affection for your kindness, but she is terrified of the town's judgment and damnation.
clues: A hidden bruise on her wrist from Aldous's rough grip.
A small wooden carving you made that she secretly keeps in her apron.
The way her eyes linger on you when Aldous isn't looking.

state.summary: Halvard, a young blacksmith in Blackwood Village, harbors a deep, forbidden love for the miller's wife, Gwenyth. While working at his anvil in the morning heat of the forge, he is interrupted by Gwenyth's harsh husband, Aldous, who demands a repair on a broken flour-chute brace and drops a sharp remark about his wife's visits.

scenes.narration:
You strike the glowing red iron on your anvil, each heavy beat of your hammer matching the throb of your heart as you look through the open doorway toward the watermill down the road. The morning air of Blackwood Fief is cool, but the forge is thick with the dry heat of burning charcoal and the sulfurous scent of coal dust. From this vantage, your eyes drift constantly to the heavy wooden wheel of the mill, churning slowly in the stream.

As you raise the hammer for another strike, a shadow falls across the threshold. It is not Gwenyth, but her husband, Aldous the Miller. He carries a bent iron flour-chute brace, his face as sour and grey as a winter sky. He drops the heavy piece of metal onto your wooden workbench with a dull thud. 'The mount broke again, blacksmith,' he grunts, not offering a greeting. 'And I need it fixed before the afternoon grinding. My wife said you were the only one who could do it proper, though I think she just likes an excuse to look down the road.' He watches you with a hard, suspicious squint, waiting to see how you respond.

You pick up the broken flour-chute brace from the workbench, your gaze dropping from Aldous's suspicious squint to the fractured iron. Without a single word, you lay your hammer against the anvil, thrust the cold brace into the hot heart of the charcoal forge, and begin to work. Under your expert strikes, the iron glows cherry-red and yields to the steady, heavy beat of your hammer, the metal fusing clean and strong once more as the miller watches in sullen silence.

Once the metal cools, Aldous snatches it up, flings a single silver penny onto the table, and leaves with a warning grumble about keeping your eyes on your work. The morning wears on, and the heat of the fire does little to warm the cold knot in your chest. By afternoon, the restlessness in your blood drives you down the muddy road toward the watermill, the heavy wheel churning the rushing stream. You find Gwenyth alone in the cool, flour-dusted shade of the millhouse, sweeping grain from the floorboards. When you speak those desperate words—confessing the love that has kept you awake for so many nights—she freezes, the broom slipping slightly in her grip. Her sad green eyes widen with sudden fear, and she looks away, her knuckles white. 'Do not say such things, Halvard,' she whispers, her voice trembling. 'I am a wedded wife, and the bailiff's eyes are always on this road. Please, go.' Before you can step closer, a heavy shadow blocks the mill doorway. Aldous stands there, his face dark with fury, having heard every word.
scenes.player_action: I fix the brace for Aldous without a word. That afternoon I carry it to the mill myself, find Gwenyth alone and tell her I love her.

scenes.narration:
You step past the towering bulk of Aldous, keeping your head low as you slip from the suffocating dust of the watermill and take the mud road back to the blacksmith forge.

For more than a week, the heavy ring of your iron hammer on the anvil becomes your only solace. You work from dawn until the red embers of the charcoal fire fade to grey, forcing all your strength into shaping glowing horseshoes and basic tools while trying to banish the memory of Gwenyth's terrified green eyes. Your calloused hands ache, but the distraction is short-lived.

On the eighth morning, the rhythmic music of your forge is cut short. A shadow falls over your threshold—not the miller, but the stern, sharp-eyed Bailiff Robert himself. He stands in your doorway, his heavy leather jerkin spotless, a massive iron-bound baton resting at his belt. Behind him in the lane, you can see Aldous pointing a thick finger at you, his sour face twisted in a smug, vindictive grin, while a few curious villagers gather to watch. 'Halvard,' the bailiff says, his voice cold and loud enough for the onlookers to hear. 'You are charged with disrupting the peace of this fiefdom and coveting another man's wife. Lay down your hammer and come with me to the hall. You will stand trial before the lord's court.'
scenes.player_action: I keep my head down and work at my forge for the next ten days.

scenes.narration:
You carefully set the heavy blacksmith hammer down on the face of the cold anvil, the iron-on-iron ringing out with a final, dying note. Taking a breath of the dry, sulfurous air, you stand quietly in your leather apron, keeping your hands open and plain to see as you look toward the doorway to hear the bailiff's demands.

You open your mouth to speak, hoping to explain your presence at the mill or at least beg for a quiet hearing, but Bailiff Robert does not give you the chance. The moment your hand leaves the hammer, he steps forward into the forge, his heavy hand coming down firmly upon your shoulder. His grip is like an iron vice, and he does not wait for an answer. 'I said lay down your tools and come, Halvard, not stand there and gawk,' Robert grunts, his stern face hardening as he pushes you toward the sunlit threshold. Outside, Aldous watches with a satisfied sneer, stepping back into the dirt road to make way for the lawman. The gathered villagers whisper and nudge one another, their eyes wide with the thrill of a scandal. The bailiff keeps his hand locked onto your shoulder, steering you firmly out of your forge and onto the muddy lane, heading toward the lord's hall.
scenes.player_action: I put down my hammer and hear him out.

choices: Beg the bailiff to hear the truth before we reach court.
Look through the crowd for any sign of Gwenyth's face.
Demand that Aldous face you himself instead of hiding behind authority.
